Abstract
—
The increasing integration of renewable energy and 
HVDC technology has significantly heightened the 
operational 
complexity of large
-
scale power systems and amplified the risk of 
voltage collapse. To enable rapid and effective voltage stability 
assessment of such highly uncertain AC/DC hybrid systems, a 
data
-
driven online probabilistic predictive framewor
k for the 
static voltage stability margin (SVSM) is proposed. A LightGBM
–
SHAP
–
KDE algorithm is developed within this framework, where 
SHAP is employed for feature selection and explanatory analysis, 
LightGBM is utilized to ensure prediction efficiency, and
 
KDE 
extends point predictions to probabilistic distributions, thereby 
enabling accurate, fast, and interpretable probabilistic SVSM 
prediction. Case studies on the modified IEEE 39
-
bus system and 
the Polish 2383
-
bus winter
-
peak system demonstrate that the
 
proposed approach achieves superior accuracy and computational 
efficiency compared with EXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), 
random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM), and also 
achieves better real
-
time performance compared with the 
traditional
 
Cumulant
-
based interval calculation method. 
Additional evaluations under PMU/WAMS data latency and 
asynchrony
,
 
topology changes, measurement noise and missing 
data further confirm the robustness and scalability of the 
proposed framework under complex oper
ating conditions.

NTRODUCTION
 
 
ITH the large
-
scale integration of renewable energy 
sources such as wind and photovoltaic generation, 
together with the extensive deployment of high
-
voltage direct current (HVDC) technology, modern power 
systems are undergoing profound structural and oper
ational 
transformations. While these developments promote 
sustainability and energy diversification, they also introduce 
new challenges to ensuring secure and stable grid operation. 
Among these challenges, static voltage stability has become 
particularly c
ritical, as the risk of voltage collapse increases 
significantly in complex AC/DC hybrid systems with high 
renewable penetration. Addressing how to maintain voltage 
stability under such conditions has become a key issue in both 
power system research and pr
actical operation [1]
.
 
The Static Voltage Stability Margin (SVSM) is widely 
used as an indicator to assess the degree of static voltage 
stability, representing the maximum load increase that a system 
can withstand under given operating conditions. With the
 
large
-
scale integration of renewable energy and the rapid 
development of AC/DC hybrid architectures, SVSM estimation 
faces new challenges, including high uncertainty, 
interdependent constraints, and stringent real
-
time 
requirements.
 
In recent years, resea
rch on SVSM evaluation has 
mainly advanced along 
the following 
directions: 
traditional 
model
-
based computation methods, deterministic data
-
driven 
prediction methods, 
and probabilistic prediction methods
.
 
 
T
raditional 
model
-
based computation methods
 
of SVSM 
include
 
Continuous Power Flow (CPF) [2], Thevenin 
Equivalent Method [3], Sensitivity Analysis Method [4], and 
Modal Analysis Method [5]. Although these methods have high 
computational accuracy and strong interpretability, they are 
complex to model
 
and have high computational costs, making 
them unsuitable for real
-
time monitoring and early warning of 
power grid operation status. 
To alleviate these drawbacks, 
several acceleration strategies have been reported, such as the 
enhanced CPF of Kim et al. [
6] and the energy
-
function 
sensitivity hybrid method of Zhang et al. [7], have accelerated 
calculations. Despite these advances, physics
-
based methods 
remain challenged by stochastic variability and frequent 
topological changes in large
-
scale systems, and 
their scalability

With the increasing deployment of wide

area 
measurement systems (WAMS) and phasor measurement units 
(PMUs), data
-
driven approaches have been widely adopted for 
online evaluation of the SVS
M. Typical methods include 
convolutional neural networks (CNNs) [8], extreme learning 
machines (ELMs) [9], and back
-
propagation neural networks 
(BPNNs) [10]. Akbari et al. proposed an optimized adaptive 
neuro
-
fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) that reduced the
 
mean 
square error by 23% on the IEEE 118
-
bus system [11]. Liu et 
al. developed a correlation
-
detection random
-
bit forest (CD
-
RBF) framework capable of margin prediction within 0.1 s, 
though its interpretability was limited [12]. Cui et al. integrated 
mult
i
-
CNN architectures with a variational Bayesian (VB) 
inference scheme to enhance voltage stability assessment [13]. 
Compared with traditional 
computation
 
methods, these 
data
-
driven
 
prediction 
m
ethod
s provide faster computation and 
stronger generalization, 
but they still struggle with inadequate 
representation of renewable energy uncertainty and limited 
interpretability
.
 
In recent years, various approaches have been proposed to 
address the uncertainty in SVSM prediction arising from 
renewable generation vari
ability. Representative techniques 
include Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) [14], probabilistic 
analysis [15], and interval analysis [16]. Q. Wang et al. [17] 
applied a probability
-
box model combined with interval
-
based 
Gram
–
Charlier expansion to characterize 
the fluctuation range 
of SVSM under variable wind and solar conditions. An 
enhanced ELM
–
KDE model was proposed in [18], where the 
distribution of power prediction errors was used to generate 
probabilistic SVSM estimates at different renewable 
penetration l
evels. T. Liu et al. [19] developed an extreme 
learning machine incorporating a Box
–
Cox transformation for 
SVSM interval prediction. While these evaluation methods 
considering uncertainty are more practical than deterministic 
data
-
driven prediction methods
, they still suffer from limited 
interpretability and have paid little attention to DC network 
constraints
.
 
As modern power systems evolve toward AC/DC hybrid 
configurations, SVSM prediction under high renewable 
penetration must not only capture 
wind
–
solar uncertainty but 
also incorporate VSC
-
HVDC control modes and DC network 
constraints. This markedly increases modeling and 
computational complexity. Ma et al. [20] developed a 
probabilistic continuation power flow model for assessing 
SVSM distribu
tion amid wind and load variation. Liu et al. [21] 
proposed a bi
-
level OPF (BLOPF) framework to estimate 
worst
-
case SVSM within converter limits, though with limited 
real
-
time capability. To improve speed, Xia et al. [2
2
] proposed 
a PPF
-
DKDE scheme for rap
id sampling and probabilistic 
density estimation in hybrid grids, while Tu et al. [2
3
] 
introduced a three
-
stage optimization using Galerkin 
parameterization for interval
-
based SVSM evaluation. 
Zhang et 
al. [24] proposed a CNN
–
LSTM
–
based framework for SVSM 
prediction in AC/DC hybrid systems with high renewable 
penetration, which demonstrated high accuracy and strong 
scalability for application to large
-
scale systems.
 
Poursaeed et 
al. [25] developed a CNN
–
BDLSTM
–
based framework for 
voltage stability assessmen
t in inverter
-
based resource (IBR)
-
dominated AC/DC systems, explicitly capturing the impacts of 
power electronic dynamics under renewable variability.
 
Overall, despite significant progress in evaluation methods 
considering uncertainty and AC/DC hybrid syst
ems, important 
challenges remain. Physics
-
based approaches are often 
computationally intensive and difficult to scale, whereas data
-
driven models frequently sacrifice interpretability. These 
limitations highlight the necessity of developing SVSM 
prediction
 
methods that are interpretable, probabilistic, and 
suitable for real
-
time application
—
providing the motivation for 
the methodology proposed in this paper
.
 
This paper proposes an online probabilistic SVSM 
prediction method for AC/DC hybrid power systems 
co
nsidering renewable energy uncertainty, namely the 
LightGBM
–
SHAP
–
KDE method. The approach leverages real
-
time operational data from power grids as model inputs and 
provides high
-
accuracy, fast, and interpretable probabilistic 
estimates of SVSM. To further 
highlight the contributions and 
innovations of this work, Table I summarizes the comparison

reported in the literature

guidance. The main contributions of this paper are as 
follows:
 
1) 
A 
data
-
driven online probabilistic prediction framework 
for SVSM in AC/DC hybrid power systems is proposed. The 
framework explicitly accounts for system uncertainty and 
AC/DC coupling characteristics while ensuring real
-
time 
performance and interpretability.
 
2) 
A 
LightGBM
–
SHAP
–
KDE method is developed within 
this framework, combining the efficient learning capability of 
LightGBM, the interpretability provided by SHAP, and the 
probabilistic modeling strength of KDE, thereby enabling 
accurate, fast, and interpre
table probabilistic SVSM prediction.
 
3) 
Extensive validation is carried out on representative test 
systems, including the IEEE 39
-
bus and the large
-
scale Polish 
2383
-
bus winter
-
peak systems, 
under PMU/WAMS latency 
and asynchrony, topology changes, measurem
ent noise, and 
missing data. Comparison with the 
Continuation Power Flow 
Method (CPF) and the Improved Cumulant Method (ICM)
 
further confirms its effectiveness, scalability, and robustness
.
